chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:
Al-Riḍā عليه السلام said: “Every road that is trodden upon or used as a pathway, whether there is a main thoroughfare in it or not, salat (prayer) should not be performed in it.”
I said, “Then where should I perform salat (prayer)?” He said, “To the right or to the left.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship
key_terms.جَادَّةٌ: a main road or clear thoroughfare
key_terms.طَرِيقٍ: a road or path used for passage
key_terms.يُتَطَرَّقُ: is taken as a route or passageway
key_terms.يُوطَأُ: is stepped on or trodden by people

ai.seo_question: Can salat (prayer) be performed on a pathway or road used by people?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the place of salat (prayer), indicating that one should not pray in a path used by passersby. It directs the worshipper to move to either side, preserving both the propriety of worship and the rights of people using the الطريق.
